GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.

GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map molecular assemblies across the Golgi interactome. The work aims to define complexes beyond the well-characterized subset, potentially revealing unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms in Golgi trafficking and homeostasis. This provides a resource for generating structural hypotheses about Golgi biology at scale.

Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.

This study takes a family-level approach to structural clustering across the tree of life, profiling the taxonomic composition of 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database. The authors identify candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and uncover a shared expansion of solenoid protein folds, expanding the known repertoire of eukaryotic signature proteins beyond what sequence-based methods can detect.

Development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors for metabolic diseases.

This preprint reports the development of selective small-molecule inhibitors targeting CYP8B1, a liver-specific cytochrome P450 enzyme that produces 12α-hydroxylated bile acids. Because elevated 12α-OH bile acids are linked to metabolic disease and gut microbiota remodeling, these inhibitors represent a potential new therapeutic strategy. The work addresses the challenge of achieving selectivity given the structural similarity of CYP8B1's active site to other cytochrome P450 enzymes.

Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.

The authors used HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling to screen 34 swine deubiquitinating enzymes for interaction with the ASFV ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L, identifying FAM105A as the top candidate. Co-immunoprecipitation experimentally confirmed the I215L–FAM105A interaction, suggesting a host factor that may modulate viral replication. This provides a structural and experimental starting point for studying host–ASFV protein interactions.

This addresses the poor activity natural enzymes show with alternative cofactors, offering a faster alternative to directed evolution and rational design. AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.

The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of the syphilis pathogen Treponema pallidum Nichols strain. This structural approach allowed functional annotation of previously uncharacterized proteins, including the ~17% of the 977 proteins lacking sequence-based functional assignment, yielding new insights into the organism's biology and pathogenic mechanisms.

Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network.

This study investigates how two structurally similar antenna subunits of photosystem II — the minor complex CP29 and the major complex LHCII — achieve functional specialization despite their structural similarity. Using 2D electronic-vibrational spectroscopy combined with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling, the authors assign spectral features to specific exciton states and reveal how subtle structural differences tune energy transfer behavior. The work provides molecular-level insight into how pigment-protein subunit diversity shapes the photosynthetic energy transfer network.

Machine Learning with Iterative Error-Driven Refinement for Predicting PFAS-Coated Surface Wettability.

By systematically sampling different PFAS head groups, the approach aims to rationalize how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic wettability, supporting the design of sustainable alternatives to persistent PFAS chemistries.

Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.

This review surveys molecular dynamics simulation methods for studying graphene and graphene-derived ionic liquid supercapacitors, focusing on how electrode charging approaches (fixed charge, constant potential, and electronic-structure-aware methods) capture interfacial structure and capacitance. It argues that molecular-scale simulation is essential because continuum theory and experiment alone cannot resolve the relevant length and time scales at these atomically defined interfaces.

Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.

This paper uses correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics to revisit a theoretical prediction that strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities can invert the intrinsic regioselectivity of electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. The authors confirm substantial energetic reordering of Wheland intermediates, supporting the concept of a 'photonic substituent effect' that can control ground-state chemical reactivity.

The information content of ultrafast observables: spectroscopy and scattering in excited norbornadiene.

This study evaluates how well different time-resolved experimental observables (photoelectron spectroscopy, electron scattering, and X-ray scattering) can distinguish between competing theoretical models of ultrafast photoisomerization in norbornadiene. The authors simulate dynamics at four levels of electronic structure theory that yield different lifetimes and branching ratios, then compute the corresponding observables. They find that the information content varies across observables, providing guidance on which techniques are most diagnostic for nonadiabatic reaction dynamics.

MARS is an open-source Python package that automates conformational sampling, infrared spectrum prediction, and microsolvation using machine-learned force fields (SO3LR, MACE) built on JAX for GPU acceleration. PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design.

This paper introduces PFM (perturbed flow matching), a generative modeling framework for structure-based drug design that overcomes the limitation of diffusion-based methods to closed-form marginal distributions. By using flow matching with a perturbed forward process, PFM allows more flexible design of the noising process, potentially improving the modeling of complex pocket-conditioned molecular distributions. The work aims to generate target-specific 3D molecules more effectively for drug discovery.

DTBNet: Multimodal 3D Geometric Perception with Hierarchical Attention for Robust Drug-Target Interaction and Binding Affinity Prediction.

DTBNet is a unified deep learning framework that predicts drug-target interactions and binding affinity by combining multimodal 3D geometric perception with hierarchical attention, rather than relying only on 1D sequences or 2D graphs. It builds heterogeneous embeddings from local chemical and structural features to better capture physicochemical interactions in 3D space, and is designed to improve generalization in cold-start scenarios where little prior data exists for a drug or target.

Recent Advances in High-Entropy Nanozymes: From Fabrication to Applications.

This review surveys high-entropy nanozymes (HEAzymes)—nanomaterials made from high-entropy alloys, oxides, sulfides, and related compounds that mimic natural enzyme catalysis. It covers fabrication strategies and applications, arguing that the multi-element complexity of high-entropy materials yields tunable, robust catalytic activity that overcomes limitations of conventional nanozymes. The field's progress is attributed to combined advances in nanotechnology, biotechnology, catalysis, and computational modeling.

Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Cofolding Models: Correct Ligand Placement Is Decoupled From Accurate Protein Conformation.

This study benchmarks four leading AI cofolding models (AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold3, Boltz-2, and Chai-1) on kinase and Class A GPCR complexes and finds that correctly placing the ligand does not guarantee that the surrounding protein structure is accurately predicted. The two aspects of prediction quality are systematically decoupled, meaning a plausible-looking ligand pose can mask a mispredicted protein fold. This cautions against judging cofolding models solely by ligand placement metrics.
